chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him):
He said: I asked him about a person in a state of janaba carrying a rakwa (small leather vessel) or a tawr (basin), and inserting his finger into it.
He said: «If his hand was impure (physically dirty), he should pour it out. And if his hand had not been touched by any impurity, he may perform ghusl from it.»
This is from what Allah the Exalted has said: «He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty.»

Then he said: «If the wudu is from abundant water in a pond or a river, there is no objection to inserting the hand into it while in any of these states of ritual impurity (ahdath), even if it has not been washed.» This points to that [ruling].

key_terms.اَلْأَحْدَاثِ: states of ritual impurity, whether minor (hadath asghar) or major (hadath akbar)
key_terms.اَلْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of major ritual impurity (janaba), obligating ghusl
key_terms.حَرَجٍ: hardship, constraint, difficulty — the term invoked from Quran 22:78 to justify ease in rulings

ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), does a person in janaba invalidate the water in a small vessel by inserting their hand into it?
ai.summary: Abu Basir posed a jurisprudential question to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about whether water in a small vessel remains valid for ghusl after a person in the state of janaba inserts their hand into it. The Imam's ruling turns on the physical cleanliness of the hand rather than the mere state of janaba, invoking Quran 22:78 to ground the principle of ease in religion (la haraj). For large bodies of water such as ponds and rivers, even an unwashed hand poses no objection.
